code_path.read_from: the installed graphrag 3.3.0 sources, 20261102 10:28 to 10:38 UTC; paths are under graphrag/ in the package
code_path.method: Standard (the default of `graphrag index`). The workflow order is in index/workflows/factory.py: load_input_documents, create_base_text_units, create_final_documents, extract_graph, finalize_graph, extract_covariates, create_communities, create_final_text_units, create_community_reports, generate_text_embeddings.
code_path.defaults_used: config/defaults.py plus the settings.yaml that `graphrag init` writes: chunking by tokens, size 1200, overlap 100, encoding o200k_base; extract_graph max_gleanings 1, entity types organization/person/geo/event; summarize_descriptions max_length 500 words, max_input_tokens 4000; community_reports max_length 2000, max_input_length 8000; cluster_graph max_cluster_size 10, use_lcc true, seed 0xDEADBEEF; claim extraction disabled; embed_text batch_size 16, batch_max_tokens 8191, three fields (entity_description, community_full_content, text_unit_text); concurrent_requests 25, async_mode threaded; cache type json on file; retry exponential_backoff (class defaults max_retries 7, base_delay 2.0); no rate limit; chat model gpt-4.1 and embedding model text-embedding-3-large (names only, the stub answers).
calls: CLI preflight (cli/index.py, index/validate_config.py): before the pipeline, one chat call 'This is an LLM connectivity test. Say Hello World' and one embedding call of one string, per configured model. `--skip-validation` skips them; graphrag.api.build_index does not make them. Measured: 1 chat call (11 prompt tokens) and 1 embedding input (9 tokens) in every run.

Extraction (index/operations/extract_graph/graph_extractor.py, GraphExtractor._process_document): one call per chunk; then for each of max_gleanings rounds one continuation call (its messages hold the whole earlier conversation: instructions, chunk, the first answer, the continue prompt), and between rounds, not after the last, a Y/N loop-check call that ends the loop on any answer other than exactly 'Y'. At the default of one gleaning that is exactly 2 calls per chunk and the loop-check is never called (measured: 47 + 47 calls for 47 chunks, 0 loop-checks). With max_gleanings g >= 2 it is 3 to 2g calls.

Description summaries (index/operations/summarize_descriptions/): after all chunks of all documents are merged, one call per entity key (title, type) and per relationship key (source, target) that has two or more distinct descriptions; a single distinct description passes through with no call. The call's input is capped at max_input_tokens (4000) less the prompt; more text means more passes for that item.
Communities (index/operations/cluster_graph.py): hierarchical Leiden on the merged graph with a fixed seed, on the largest connected component only (use_lcc true). No model call.

Community reports (index/operations/summarize_communities/): one call per community at every level, deepest level first, each asking for a JSON report through response_format (json_schema). A community's prompt holds its entity and relationship rows if they fit in max_input_length (8000 tokens); if not, they are replaced by the reports of its sub-communities. A report that fails to parse is logged and left out; there is no retry beyond the transport retry.

Embeddings (index/workflows/generate_text_embeddings.py, index/operations/embed_text/): after the graph and reports exist, three fields are embedded one after another: entity title plus description, community report full text, chunk text. A call holds at most 16 inputs and at most 8191 tokens (counted with the embedding model's tokenizer), so long chunks make smaller batches.

Cache (cache/, graphrag_llm/middleware/with_cache.py): a JSON file cache keyed on the call's arguments, on by default, covering chat and embedding calls. Measured: re-running the same 20 documents from the cache that run b-n20 left made 1 chat call and 1 embedding input in total, the two preflight calls.

Request bodies seen by the stub carry only model and messages (reports add response_format; embeddings add encoding_format float). No max_tokens, no temperature: the reply length is not capped by the client at these defaults.

per_chunk_or_per_document: extraction and gleaning (2 calls per chunk, prompt does not depend on any other document)
corpus_level: merging entities and relationships across every chunk of every document, then description summaries (calls only for items seen with 2 or more distinct descriptions anywhere in the corpus)
graph finalisation and Leiden clustering on the whole graph, keeping the largest connected component only
community reports (calls = communities at all levels; prompt text depends on the graph and on lower-level reports)
entity-description embeddings and report embeddings (row counts come from the two steps above)
corpus_level_vs_per_chunk.consequence: Calls at N documents are not N times the calls at 1 document. `graphrag update` (incremental) exists in the CLI and was not run.

depends_on_the_model: Gleaning loop-check calls: none at the default of one gleaning; with two or more, each depends on whether the reply is exactly 'Y'.

Prompt tokens of the continuation call: it carries the first answer, so it grows with the length of the model's first reply (measured 128,268 / 131,182 / 144,793 total prompt tokens for the same 47 continuation calls under shapes A / A2 / B).
Number of summary calls: set by how many entities and relationships the model names and how often it describes the same one in two different ways.

Number of communities and so of report calls: set by the graph the model produced (largest connected component only), at every level. Measured 3, 4 and 54 reports for 1, 5 and 20 documents under shape B, which is an effect of that shape's graph, not a rate.
Prompt tokens of report calls and the substitution of sub-community reports when a community's rows exceed 8000 tokens: never reached under these shapes (largest report prompt 2637 tokens).
Whether the run finishes: if no chunk yields any entity, or none any relationship, the pipeline stops after extraction (measured under shape A, exit 1).
Output tokens everywhere: unmeasured; the stub's completion token counts are the length of the stub's own fixed answers.

Retries and failed calls: a call that errors is retried by the transport middleware (up to 7 times at the class default); an extraction call that still fails yields an empty graph for that chunk and the run goes on. Not exercised, the stub never fails.

The first extraction call's prompt tokens and the number of extraction and gleaning calls (at the default) do not depend on any answer: 126,435 prompt tokens and 47 calls for the 47 chunks, identical under all three shapes.
Embedding inputs for chunks (47) do not depend on answers; for entities and reports they do.
hand_recorded.tokenizer_note: Prompt and completion tokens in `measured` are the stub's tiktoken cl100k_base counts, not any provider's. GraphRAG's own chunking and budgets use o200k_base and the litellm tokenizer; chunk sizes quoted from its output are in o200k_base tokens.

outbound_findings.attempts_seen: Exactly one, in the diagnostic run b-n1-sink where HTTPS_PROXY pointed at a local sink that records and refuses: CONNECT raw.githubusercontent.com:443. It is LiteLLM fetching its model price table when it is imported (log line: 'Failed to fetch remote model cost map from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/main/model_prices_and_context_window.json ... Falling back to local backup'). In every run with the refusing proxy on port 9 the same single warning line appears. LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True turns the fetch off (litellm/litellm_core_utils/get_model_cost_map.py, read 20261102); it was left unset on purpose so the attempt would show.
outbound_findings.telemetry: A search of graphrag and its seven sibling packages for telemetry, posthog, appinsights and opentelemetry found nothing (case-insensitive grep over the eight packages' .py files, 20261102 10:50 UTC). Absence in the source is not proof for the dependencies' behaviour at run time; the sandbox below is what rules outbound traffic out.
outbound_findings.enforcement: Besides the proxy variables, each builder process ran under a macOS sandbox-exec profile denying every outbound connection except to loopback. The runner proves the profile first: loopback connects, an RFC 5737 documentation address returns PermissionError. sandbox-exec is deprecated by Apple but worked on this machine.

measured.settings: the file `graphrag init --model gpt-4.1 --embedding text-embedding-3-large` writes, plus one api_base line per model pointing at the stub
measured.document_input: the `body` of each article, one .txt file each, in documents.tsv order, first N

shapes.B: Per chunk the first answer holds 6 entities and 5 relationships; the gleaning answer adds none (it is just the completion marker); a loop-check answer is 'N'; a description summary is a fixed one-sentence text; a community report is a fixed-size JSON report with 5 findings. Entity names are the 6 capitalised words of the chunk with the smallest SHA-256, so chunks that share words share entities. Each entity's type is one of the 4 default types picked from the hash of its name, so a repeated name always has the same type. The 5 relationships chain the 6 entities in hash order, with a weight of 5 to 9 from the hash of the pair. Every description carries the chunk's SHA-256 prefix, so the same entity or pair seen in two chunks gets two different descriptions (which is what makes GraphRAG's summarisation step fire).
shapes.A: Every extraction and gleaning answer is the bare completion marker: no entities, no relationships. The connectivity test answer is 'Hello World'.
shapes.A2: Supplementary, not the brief's shape A: every extraction answer is the same 2 entities and 1 relationship with identical descriptions (the smallest answer that lets this pipeline complete); the gleaning answer is the completion marker. Community reports are the same fixed-size JSON report as in shape B.
